# TDPdf v1.24.0.0

**Application Insights is removed. TDPdf now reports to one OpenTelemetry collector, and carries no telemetry destination inside the binary at all.**

Both destinations ran side by side for two weeks. Azure received a lossy subset of roughly one event in six — installs and heartbeats, none of the interaction events — while the collector carried the full stream, including the evidence that identified the text editor defect fixed in 1.23.7.0. A second destination that saw less and cost more had no case left.

## What this changes for administrators

**The Intune detection rule now requires 1.24.0.0, so managed machines pick this up on the next evaluation. Assignments are unaffected.**

The telemetry remediation script no longer writes an Application Insights connection string, and now deletes the retired `ConnectionString` value from the policy key. That value is a live Azure ingestion secret; leaving it unread in the registry on every managed device was not worth preserving. Upgrading also deletes any `%ProgramData%\TDPdf\telemetry.dat` left behind by an older install, for the same reason.

Nothing about the collector configuration changes. `OtlpEndpoint` and `OtlpToken` under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\TDPdf\Telemetry` are unchanged, and `TDPdf.exe /clear-telemetry` works exactly as before — it still outranks the managed policy rather than racing it.

**Nothing is deleted on the Azure side by this release.** The existing resource keeps its data and simply stops receiving.

## The embedded key is gone

Released binaries no longer carry an encrypted destination compiled into the executable. That mechanism obfuscated a secret inside a binary shipped to end-user laptops — a speed bump rather than a control — and rotating it required building, signing and shipping a new version to every device, which is why it was never once rotated. The destination now arrives only by administrator-pushed policy, so rotation is a remediation cycle.

`TDPdf.exe /set-telemetry` and its DPAPI-encrypted file are removed with it. There is no longer a secret for an operator to enter by hand.

## Privacy

Reports carry the machine name as `host.name`. Azure's SDK populated this by default and the OpenTelemetry default does not, so it is now set explicitly rather than being lost along with the destination — it is what separates one machine with a fault from a fleet-wide regression. It remains the only identifying field in the payload, and it is documented in `PRIVACY.md`, which has been rewritten for this release along with `NOTICE` and the administrator guide.

Document contents, file names, paths, form values, search terms and signature images are never sent, and the per-launch session identifier is still never written to disk.

## Verifying this download

The executable is signed by *The Doodle Project Code Signing*, a private certificate. On managed machines that trust it, the signature validates. On a machine that does not, Windows will still warn on first run. Use `SHA256SUMS.txt` to confirm the download independently.
